about: The one fight V3 plays: the first career fight of a frankendom.com page load at 82a994d15 (V1 main.ts + match.ts begin('career')): the Centurion at the Match's default level (PRESET_LEVEL.normal = level-anchor-defs.json normal, 18: V1 only moves to the career level on a rematch, and a rematch that changes his loadout reloads the page, so a guest always meets him at 18 with the gladius and scutum), met at a guest's tier (Recruit), the Match's default seed, the longsword, SPECIAL 1/2 from career-rules.json betaCut slot defaults, specials on (rows80 specialsFromLevel 1), the default stance pick (stance.ts PICKS[0]). Rematch steps the seed as V1 nextSeed does. tempoHz: V1's default tempo (main.ts TEMPO_KEY). frameDtMaxS: the most one frame injects into the sim (V1 first-loss-rules.json frame-dt-max-s). gfx: V1's gfx lift (fx-rows gfx.default on). Dom 2026-10-26 (later): the opponent keeps the Minotaur's look but fights as V1's Pitborn (`opponent`): the Pitborn's moves, cleaver (at every level), stats, AI profile under the `ai` brain row and class special (Earth Fold at 18), no shield and no shield-bearer block; the same level, seed and picks. ?pitborn=v1 (and ?foe=v1) = the Centurion's fight above exactly (`opponentV1`, src/fight/foe-pick.ts).

camera.about: V2's lower, over-the-shoulder fight camera on V1's lock (src/fight/camera.ts setLockFrame; ?cam=v1 = V1's lock exactly). V2 (Frankendom-v2 data/camera.json portrait: back 6.5, up 2.8, side 1.0, zoom 0.9) puts the eye ~2.8 m up and 1.0 m over the right shoulder; V1's lock at a 2.5 m gap is 4.2 m up (max(lockLiftFloor 3.2, gap x 1.3) x fightBack 1.3) and 5.7 m back. lift scales V1's lock height (2.8 / 4.2); side is V2's shoulder step in metres. A finish eases both back to V1's lock, as V1 does fightBack. zoom (Dom 2026-10-27, 'the camera is still a bit far out ... just add 10%'): the lens, 1.1 = everything 10% larger on screen about the frame centre (vertical field of view 51 deg -> 2 atan(tan 25.5 deg / zoom), src/fight/camera-zoom.ts, scene.ts); 1 = the camera exactly as before; limits 0.5..2. ?zoom=1 reverts on a phone without a deploy, ?zoom=1.1 is the row, any value in the limits works. Presentation only.

wide.about: Dom 2026-10-27 (phone, landscape): the fight looked zoomed OUT, the hero and bosses tiny in a wide field of sand, where portrait is right. The lock's distance is already fitted by the vertical field (V1's min(aspect, 1)), so the hero is the same SHARE of the screen height in every shape; but a landscape phone is 375 px tall, so that share is 2.6x fewer pixels than on a portrait phone (measured: hero 0.35 of the height engaged on 375x812 = 282 px, 0.28 on 812x375 = 106 px). So a wide screen gets an extra lens zoom: 1 below fromAspect (every portrait phone and tablet: portrait is exactly as it was), `zoom` from toAspect (landscape phones and desktop), linear between; the horizontal field never passes maxHfovDeg on an ultra-wide. src/fight/camera-zoom.ts wideBoost, scene.ts applies it on every resize. ?wide=<n> (1..2) replaces zoom for a page load, ?wide=v1 = no wide-screen zoom. Presentation only.

pitch.about: Zone follow camera pitch (Dom 2026-10-27: a skyline band should show under the HUD on a phone; at the default pitch the true horizon sits at the very top edge of the portrait screen). `default` is the preset a page load uses: 'off' = the camera exactly as it was. A preset is the angle (degrees) the view axis looks down, flatter = more horizon; the eye height follows so the hero keeps his screen position (heroY: the point on him that stays put; minEyeY: the eye never drops below). ?pitch=low (or flat, soft, or any number inside limits) switches the zone camera on a phone with no deploy; ?pitch=off is the default. Zone only: the single fight (?postkill=v1) never reads this. A finish eases back to the default frame, so the finishers and their tour are untouched; the multi-boss widen is applied first and the pitch follows it. Presentation only.

specialPace.about: Dom 2026-10-26 after playing: 'the skull crack is good, but it's a bit slowed down ... maybe 25% faster. The whirlwind speed is fine.' The player's SKULL CRACK (SPECIAL 1, skill cleave) runs at `scale` of its V1 ticks, each rounded to the nearest tick (src/fight/special-pace.ts): committed windup 32 -> 24 (sandbox specialMeleeWindup), no-attack recovery after the strike 45 -> 34 (rules special.recovery), the clip's raise and return read over 120 -> 90 and 45 -> 34 so the Special_SkullCrack clip plays the same span 4/3 faster, the start whoosh 280 -> 210 ms. Damage, reach, cooldown and the cast pushback are unchanged. The Whirlwind (SPECIAL 2) and every opponent special keep V1's timing. ?skull=v1 = today's timing.

specialTerms.about: Dom 2026-10-26 (via Lead): 'Specials, all of them, can be used every 9 seconds, no stamina cost.' The HERO's specials (SPECIAL 1 the Skull Crack, SPECIAL 2 the Whirlwind, and a plain skill if the hero carries one) cool for `cooldown` ticks (540 = 9 s at 60 Hz), counted as today (the Skull Crack from the strike's release, the Whirlwind from the press), and cost and need `stamina` (0) instead of their move row's (the Whirlwind's 40). Kept: the first special ready 2 s in (rows80 first), the Skull Crack's 2.2 m reach and its no-attack recovery after the strike, exhaustion (an empty bar still refuses every attack), a spell's own cost. Opponents' specials are unchanged. src/fight/special-terms.ts; off in headless runs (Gate 0). ?spec=v1 = V1's cooldowns (6 s Skull Crack, 15 s Whirlwind) and the Whirlwind's 40 stamina.

readyRing.about: Dom 2026-10-26: 'a thin yellow extra circle around it, not fat, that glows a little when you can use it.' blendMs.about: PM queue item (a), 'roll blend' (PLAN step-5 list): V2 #70's per-transition blend rows, numbers as they are in Frankendom-v2 data/anim.json blendMs (main 78d19d6; V2 render.js combatOf). V1 (characters.ts) fades a combat clip in over the first 1/12 and out over the last 1/10 of its move whatever the move's length, and eases every clip weight at 24/s. With these rows a combat clip's weight rises over `<kind>In` ms after its move starts and falls over `<kind>Out` ms before it ends: attack (every swing and the kick), special (a special's windup + recovery), hurt (a hit reaction), roll; `locomotion` is the time an eased weight (walk, run, guard, every clip) takes to close ~95% of its gap (V1's 24/s is 125 ms). None above 150 ms (V2's A1 cap). Deaths, finishers, the draw, guard/block/parry/deflect and the live-blade snap keep V1's. Both fighters, visual only (src/fight/anim-blend.ts). ?blend=v1 = V1's transitions exactly.

settleMs.about: V2's one named exception to the 150 ms cap (Frankendom-v2 data/anim.json settleMs, Dom 2026-10-26 on V2: the roll 'suddenly switches to the normal stance'): the roll's weight eases out over this many ms before it ends, in place of blendMs.rollOut, so the roll settles into the stance instead of snapping. V2 set 300 for its 84-tick (1.4 s) roll-to-run, where 300 ms is the last 21 %; V3's roll is V1's 36 ticks (600 ms), where 300 ms is the whole second half and she rose while the sim still had her rolling (Lead 2026-10-26, on PR #35's stills). So 120 here: V2's rollOut, the same ~20 % tail of a 36-tick roll, and recovery reads where the sim recovers. ?blend=v1 = V1's.

The build (scripts/blade-tables.mjs) bundles only these; the source file stays V1's as copied. test/blade-tables.test.mjs pins that every weapon the fight can reach is listed. The scythe STAYS (the Gargantua freeze, #193: the build had cut it and bladeFrames threw inside stepDuel): ?bossweapon=v1 and any spawn without a boss-weapons row still fight the executioner with it; test/blade-tables.test.mjs checks every data/profiles.json row at every level.

foeReach.about: Dom 2026-10-26 on his phone: the opponent's attacks hurt him from too far away. Only for `opponent` drawn in `body`: ?pitborn=v1 (the Centurion, gladius) and ?foe=v1 (V1's bodies) keep V1's sweeps. `?<query>=<v1>` (?reach=v1) = V1's cleaver sweeps exactly (the hero is on V1's sweeps by default already; ?reach=clip still moves only the hero's). foeSpecialReach.about: Dom 2026-10-26: the Minotaur's special landed (hit sound, the hero's reaction, 30 damage) from any distance, 3.5 m included: 'the distance isn't matching the reactions.' V1's rule gave an opponent's melee special the full rules reach (3.0 m) to start and no check at release; the player's picked special has had 2.2 m / 2.6 m. With `on` 1 an opponent's plain MELEE special (not a spell, a bow volley or a cone breath; his heavies are untouched) is pressed (src/fight/ai.ts and the sim's gate in duel.ts) only inside `start` metres, and when its release tick arrives with the hero farther than `release` metres it fizzles: SpecialFizzled, no damage, no hit pose, no hit sound. The values are the player's own (sandbox specialMeleeReach 2.2 m, + specialMeleeSlack 0.4 m). src/fight/foe-special-reach.ts; off in headless runs (Gate 0 and the V3-only golden rows). ?special=v1 = V1's reach (3.0 m, no release check). `on` 0 = off.

The shared rows are not edited (they also drive every opponent and boss special). Windup pose, ready ring, impact tints stay. heroMana.about: Dom 2026-10-28: 'remove mana for now'. The HERO has no mana: no MANA bar on the HUD (the STAMINA bar keeps the whole row) and no mana cost or gate on a spell, a heal or the staff's bolt, so they are free and held only by their own ~9 s cooldown (specialTerms) and the ready ring. `mana: false` = off. Opponents are untouched: the foes' spells and missiles still carry and spend their own pool (Dom: keep the opponent spells). src/fight/hero-mana.ts; off in headless runs (Gate 0). ?mana=v1 = the MANA bar and the mana cost, as before.

knockRound.about: Audit C 2026-10-29: a blow's shove is whole steps, rounded. V1 looped `k < knockback`, so a fractional knockback (a glancing off-band blow's knockback x 0.4) shoved one step too many: a thrust of 3 shoved ceil(1.2) = 2, a kick of 6 shoved ceil(2.4) = 3, a sliver under half a step still shoved one and could count as a wall impact. `round: true` = Math.round (1.2 -> 1, 2.4 -> 2, 0.4 -> 0: no shove, no wall impact; a whole number is unchanged), like the two special-reaction shoves in duel.ts. `round: false` = V1's ceil. src/fight/knock-round.ts; off in headless runs (Gate 0 steps V1's numbers). ?knock=v1 = V1's shove.
